trial_court: Court of Ld. Additional District Judge, Contai, Matrimonial Suit Number 145 of 2005
case_name: Chandan Kumar Bera vs Atasi Bera
facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent are husband and wife. Petitioner filed an application under Section 13 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for decree of divorce on the ground of cruelty and desertion. The trial court dismissed the suit.

legal_principles.principle: Where parties are living separately for several years and their reunion is not possible, the court can pass a decree of divorce.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically stated that where parties are living separately for several years and their reunion is not possible, the court can pass a decree of divorce.
cited_cases: Gurbux Singh Vs. Harminder Kaur, (2010) 14 SCC 301
R. Srinivas Kumar Vs. R. Shametha, (2019) 9 SCC 409
Munish Kakkar Vs. Nidhi Kakkar, (2020) 14 SCC 657
use_in: divorce cases where parties are living separately for several years

legal_principles.principle: A court can pass a decree of divorce if the parties have been living separately and there is no chance of their reunion.
legal_principles.held: Nothing remains in this marital tie. So, he prayed for decree of divorce.
cited_cases: Gurbux Singh Vs. Harminder Kaur, (2010) 14 SCC 301
R. Srinivas Kumar Vs. R. Shametha, (2019) 9 SCC 409
Munish Kakkar Vs. Nidhi Kakkar, (2020) 14 SCC 657
use_in: divorce cases where parties are living separately and there is no chance of their reunion

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the decree of divorce is granted to the petitioner.
